title: Reduction of the ind-etale lift
statement:
For the lift $C=H_A(\overline C)$ of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], the
specified map $C/IC\to\overline C$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the existing construction H=ClosedLift A C, J=I.map(algebraMap A H), R=H/J, and its specified reduction map. The quotient scalar-tower instances make it an A/I-algebra map r:R -> C; its commutation with A/I is checked on quotient representatives. Filteredness gives the existing indEtale instance for H.

For c in C choose a representative b in an etale stage P_i of an ind-etale presentation of C. Apply Algebra.exists_etale_coefficientLift to obtain an etale A-algebra L.LiftRing, reduction L.reduction and its specified quotient isomorphism e. Choose a quotient representative a of e.symm b. Regard L.reduction as an A-algebra map by checking coefficients using polynomialReduction; compose with P_i -> C. Present L.LiftRing by exists_index, so a gives an element of H mapping to c. The private helper surjective_toAlgHom proves this; taking its class in R proves surjectivity of r.

Base change of H to A/I is ind-etale by RingHom.IndEtale.isStableUnderBaseChange.tensorProduct. Transport this along Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor to R via ObjectProperty.ind.prop_of_iso. Both R and C are now ind-etale over A/I. RingHom.IndEtale.of_comp and r.commutes make r ind-etale. Algebra.IndEtale.weaklyEtale then gives flatness of C as an R-module for the algebra structure induced by r. These are the existing library base-change, relative-map and weak-etaleness clauses, without importing the bundled principal-Zariski stability theorem.

Let K=ker r. By surjectivity, Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective identifies R/K with C as R-algebras. Transport flatness with Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv, so K is pure. Ideal.exists_eq_mul_of_pure gives, for each x in K, an e in K with x=x*e.

Prove the required unit-lifting property locally, since the existing ClosedLiftUnits module imports ClosedLift and cannot be imported here. For y in H whose image is a unit, take a representative b in an etale stage X. The map X.alg -> C extends to Localization.Away b via IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom. This localization is etale over A and hence has a presentation-model object Y by exists_index. The localization map conjugated by that presentation is an arrow X -> Y. The colimit cocone equation identifies y with the image of b/1 at Y; since b/1 is a unit there, y is a unit. This is the complete private helper isUnit_of_isUnit_image, valid for every input A-algebra C.

Lift e from step 4 to y in H. Since r(e)=0, toAlgHom(y)=0 and toAlgHom(1-y)=1. Step 5 makes 1-y a unit in H, hence 1-e a unit in R. The equation x=x*e gives x*(1-e)=0, and IsUnit.mul_left_eq_zero gives x=0. Thus r is injective and, with step 2, bijective. All constructions include the zero ring and arbitrary ideals; no nilpotence or nontriviality is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem bijective_reduction [Algebra.IndEtale (A ⧸ I) C] :
    Function.Bijective (reduction A C I)
lean.note: Exact existing theorem: reduction is the quotient factorization of the retained map toAlgHom; bijectivity of this ring homomorphism is equivalent to its being an isomorphism. Ambient variables bind arbitrary commutative rings A and C, an ideal I, compatible A and A/I algebra structures, and no nilpotence assumption.
